name: notion-company-to-linear-customer

trigger.trigger_note: Notion POLLING trigger on Companies, watching the Deals relation (property id giUg), same as the classic Zap. Durable triggers have no polling-interval field, so it polls at the account default — matching the classic Zap's polling_interval_override of 0. No external URL to cut over.

notion.note: Guard + write-back property: Companies 'Linear Customer ID' (rich_text). NOTE: the classic Zap's mapping left DOMAINS in this property on existing records (e.g. tanninroad.com.au) instead of Linear customer UUIDs — the guard treats any non-empty value as 'already in Linear', so those records are unaffected; the durable writes real UUIDs going forward.

linear.note: domains gets the bare hostname parsed out of the Companies Website url (the classic Zap passed the raw url); externalIds gets the COM-n unique id read off the page (the classic Zap read the same value from [Table] Company IDs).

tables.01JM8PH8YM93A482M8BFZ6WKW6: [Table] Company IDs — NOT read by this workflow. The classic Zap looked up f11/f7 here; the durable reads the COM-n id and the guard off the Notion page itself, and notion-companies-to-zapier-table mirrors the written id back into f7.

replaces_classic_zap: Company Linked to Deal -> Create Customer in Linear

cutover.classic_zap_disabled: 2026-08-10 — confirmed by Dennis. Not machine-verifiable: classic Zaps are exposed by neither the SDK CLI nor the MCP connector. Race with the classic Zap is now moot.
cutover.status: complete — this durable is the only thing creating Linear customers from Notion

description: Notion Companies polling trigger (Deals relation changed) -> create the company as a Linear customer (bare-domain + COM-n external id), write the customer id back to the Company.
